races.name: Queen Mary Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Alta Regina
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Good, but as a true prominent type displaced into a deeper midfield slot by the sheer volume of pace in this field, James McDonald will need to work hard to recover her natural racing position early.|
runners_data.comment: Alta Regina arrives on the back of a deeply impressive debut success, winning with 4¼ lengths in hand at Lingfield, and the combination of proven effectiveness at today's trip on good-to-firm and a high draw that can prove advantageous here make her a leading contender; the sole query is whether that single run leaves her exposed.

runners_data.name: Armor Supreme
runners_data.note: Twice placed over 5f Good before winning, so she handles conditions and has consistency; Rossa Ryan rides, but her prominent style is compromised by the crowded pace map, meaning she may not get the rail position her game demands.|
runners_data.comment: Unlucky not to win in Listed company last time, going down by a head at York, and that run confirms smart ability over today's trip and going; the rise in weight and high draw from stall 19 are the checks to consider.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: Showed versatility when third at 6f before winning over 5f Good five days ago for P Twomey; the quick reappearance is worth monitoring, and while she wants to race prominent, the pace glut means P J McDonald may be riding a reactive rather than proactive race.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a good attitude to win a novice at York by a short-head last time out, and acts on the ground with the right distance profile, but cheekpieces are added here suggesting improvement is needed to compete at this level on a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good on latest start for Richard Hughes after a third on debut, so she arrives in form; Hector Crouch picks up the ride, and she is a genuine prominent type who may find herself squeezed for position by the weight of similar rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by four lengths in a novice here last time in the style of a horse with plenty more to offer, and return to this course and distance on good ground looks ideal; the main risk is the 40-day absence.

runners_data.name: Celtic Dispute
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Firm for Patrick Biancone and wears a hood, which may assist concentration in a chaotic 28-runner dash; the blinkers note is relevant in a field where early focus is at a premium, though simulated going data is limited to Firm rather than Good.|
runners_data.comment: Winning a 2yo Gulfstream Park contest by a neck on its latest start suggests a sound attitude, and it handles fast ground over 5f well; the first-time blinkers may sharpen things further, though 39 days off and a field of this depth provide the checks.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Unknown style tag with only two runs to her name, both on Good ground where she twice finished placed; David Egan rides for Kevin Philippart De Foy, and with no win yet she needs things to fall right, though her consistency over the course and distance is a minor plus.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but showed decent debut level when runner-up at Carlisle, beaten 10 lengths by an impressive winner; effective at 5f on a sound surface, though the rating of 108 suggests he faces a stiff task from stall 27 carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Crystal Queen
runners_data.note: Winner then second over 5f Good for Richard and Peter Fahey, with Colin Keane booked — a high-quality jockey-trainer combination that knows how to place horses in big-field sprints; she is a natural prominent type whose redistribution into a busier mid-pack role slightly dilutes her chance.|
runners_data.comment: Improved markedly on debut when scoring with plenty in hand at Beverley last time, and acts on today's trip and going — a lightly raced filly with more to offer, though she faces a stiff step up in class here.

runners_data.name: Drazinda
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Heavy for Graffard and Barzalona, so the step up to Good To Firm is an unresolved question mark; she is a prominent-style runner shown at the rear of the map due to the field's pace density, making going suitability the primary concern here.|
runners_data.comment: Broke her duck with a promising debut win at Chantilly, and there's likely more improvement to come — but this sharp step up in grade on different ground tests the limits of that single run.

runners_data.name: Envision
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good latest, having finished fourth on debut, with Silvestre De Sousa riding and a hood fitted; she is an authentic prominent racer who will be shuffled wider and deeper than ideal by the sheer number of similar types, so her effectiveness depends on whether she can recover a forward berth.|
runners_data.comment: Blinkers clearly sparked a smart 4-length Windsor novice win last time, and Envision is proven over today's trip and going, but stepping up markedly in grade from stall 12 at 128lb, this outsider on our figures looks up against it.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: Twice placed over 5f Good for Andrew Balding, still seeking a first win; Rob Hornby rides and she handles conditions, but as a genuine prominent type displaced into a crowded mid-pack slot she needs more than consistency to win this from a disadvantaged position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked 24th of 27 on our figures, Fast Track faces a stiff rise in class despite a short-head second at Nottingham last time; effective at today's trip on good ground and a top course trainer keeps connections alive.

runners_data.name: Havana Lightning
runners_data.note: Bounced back from a fifth-place debut to win over 5f Good, which shows resilience; Billy Loughnane is a powerful rider in big-field sprints, and while she is a natural pace horse the traffic conditions mean she will likely have to make do with a position that does not suit.|
runners_data.comment: Improved from debut to win a novice at Yarmouth last time but steps into much deeper waters here, and ranked 22nd of 27 on our figures, it's hard to make a case — though effective at today's trip on good ground and likely not yet the finished article.

runners_data.name: Kentucky Rain
runners_data.note: Only run produced a second over 5f Good, so limited evidence to assess, and her style is genuinely unknown; Cieren Fallon rides for Lemos De Souza, and the redistribution to the rear reflects the lack of pace-committed form rather than any tactical choice.|
runners_data.comment: Promising on debut — a runner-up beaten 1¼ lengths at Goodwood over today's trip — Kentucky Rain arrives 26 days later with scope to improve, but from stall 9 carrying 128 lb, our figures rank it 20th of 27 and it rates a no-hoper at this level.

runners_data.name: Love A Giggle
runners_data.note: Dual winner over 5f including on Standard ground, so her form is consistent; Clifford Lee rides for Karl Burke, but her natural prominent style is further compromised than most by the redistribution to a hold-up position, making this a significantly harder assignment than her record might suggest.|
runners_data.comment: Backs up debut success with a Listed win at York last time, quickening gamely from an unpredictable pace, and with today's yard boasting a strong record in this race, this progressive filly looks to have more to offer — though stepping up to 6f for the first time is the one unknown.

runners_data.name: Lover Girl
runners_data.note: Three runs show a sequence of 3-1-1, with wins on Standard and Good surfaces, for Kevin Philippart De Foy; Rowan Scott rides, and of the prominent-style runners she has enough experience and course-distance form to hold a clean handy position if she breaks well.|
runners_data.comment: Backed up back-to-back wins with a gutsy Listed third last time out, and her sharp early pace and proven effectiveness at today's trip and going give her every chance from stall 4 — though that front-running style could again prove her undoing if she burns too bright.

runners_data.name: Magic Effort
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Good before finishing fourth, so she has a reverse trajectory into this; Benoit De La Sayette rides for Ismail Mohammed, and while the debut win is noted, the subsequent backward step makes her a bigger risk at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Showed debut-level form when beaten five lengths in a novice latest, and carrying a penalty into a field of 27 makes this a steep ask — a nice prospect, but this looks beyond her at this stage.

runners_data.name: Miss Lizzy
runners_data.note: Form string of 7-4-1-5 tells a mixed story, including a win at 6f Standard but defeats at this track; Paddy Bradley rides, and the headgear note (tongue tie) is relevant, though the inconsistency of her record sets a higher bar in a race this competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of 27 on our figures, Miss Lizzy is almost certainly crying out for a return to further than today's trip, making this assignment a tough sell despite decent recent form and an eye-catching first-time hood.

runners_data.name: More Champagne
runners_data.note: Debut winner for Thomas Morley with John Velazquez in the saddle, but going is listed as unknown and she has been off 54 days; the combination of unknown ground suitability and longest absence in the field adds meaningful uncertainty to what could otherwise be an intriguing runner.|
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut, winning by 6½ lengths at Keeneland over 5f on fast ground, and US-trained runners have a solid record in this race — but 54 days off the track and ranked 14th in a deep 27-runner field gives cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Niewiadoma
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Good before finishing ninth, which is a red flag heading into this; Luke Morris rides for Archie Watson, and the dramatic reversal of form on the same going needs explaining before she can be trusted at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way out chasing a fast pace up in class at Listed level last time, Niewiadoma needs a significant bounce-back here and looks hard to fancy ranked near the foot of the weights on our figures, though the 5f trip and good going suit.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Progressive record of 3-2-1, winning over 5f Good most recently, for Richard Hannon with Sean Levey; she is the type to navigate a hectic early pace and arrive with momentum, and Hannon's record in big-field juvenile sprints adds weight to her claims.|
runners_data.comment: Broke her duck at Goodwood last time but, ranked 21 of 27 on our figures, she has plenty to find here, and carrying 128 lb from stall 23 adds to the task for this sharp juvenile.

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.note: Form reads 1-5-3 with the win coming on Soft, and both Good-ground runs have been less convincing; Daniel Tudhope rides for David O'Meara, and the going switch to Good To Firm is the key question given her best effort came under softer conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Ran a solid race when a close third in a Listed contest at Sandown 20 days ago, ridden patiently with every chance, and acts on the going and has form over today's trip; a scopey type with potential upside, though stall 20 and a mark of 128 lb are the constraints here.

runners_data.name: Ruiva
runners_data.note: Debut winner for Wesley Ward with Juan Hernandez up, going unknown, wearing blinkers and off 49 days; Ward's Ascot juvenile record commands respect, but the combination of unknown going, significant absence and unfamiliar track means she carries more unknowns than the market will fully price.|
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut but faces a significant step up in class; the first-time blinkers and a trainer with a proven record in this race are in her favour, though 49 days off the track and a wide draw from stall 16 are factors to weigh against the striking seven-length winning margin she posted at Churchill Downs.

runners_data.name: Senorita Bonita
runners_data.note: Impressive debut winner over 5f Good for Simon and Ed Crisford with William Buick in the saddle — one of the best jockey-trainer pairings in the race; she ran just 14 days ago, handles this going, and has the gate speed to secure a natural prominent position without fighting for it.|
runners_data.comment: Pleasing debut winner at Nottingham over this trip who showed a good attitude to score on good ground, and top connections suggest more improvement is likely — though stepping up sharply in grade from a single start is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good on debut for Harry Eustace with Dylan Browne McMonagle booked — a young jockey who has thrived in big-field races; limited evidence but the profile of a gate-sharp filly who can find a clean position quickly makes her relevant in the lead-dominant scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Promising debut winner at Salisbury over today's trip on good ground, and there's potential for more — but stepping up markedly in grade from a single run, and ranked 26th of 27 on our figures, makes it very hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Shining Moment
runners_data.note: Ran 2-1 in two starts with Oisin Murphy up for Wesley Ward, wearing blinkers; Murphy's big-race experience is a clear asset in a 28-runner sprint, and Ward's fillies have historically travelled well to Ascot, making her the stronger of the two US raiders on form.|
runners_data.comment: Showed significant improvement to score with plenty in hand at Churchill Downs last time, and the combination of proven 5f speed on a fast surface and a trainer with a strong record in this race make Shining Moment hard to dismiss, though first-time blinkers and draw 21 add unknowns.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Won over 5f both on Good and Soft for P Twomey, with a fourth at 6f also on the card; W J Lee rides and the versatility of going is a small positive on a day the ground is riding Good To Firm, though she faces stiff competition from stablemate Big Negotiator.|
runners_data.comment: Velozee showed real smartness when winning back-to-back before a below-par effort at Naas when the race may have come too soon; now fresher over an ideal 5f trip with a trainer in form, a bounce-back looks well within reach — though that 7-length defeat is the key risk to overcome.

runners_data.name: Victorious
runners_data.note: Dual winner at 6f Good for Aidan O'Brien with Ryan Moore — the standout jockey-trainer combination in the race; stepping down from 6f to 5f, she has the class and tactical intelligence of her connections to find a clean prominent position and quicken off it, making her profile arguably the most complete in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Successive wins culminate in a Naas Group 3 last time, where she found more when pressed — the yard won this 12 months ago and a top course jockey takes the ride, but stepping back to 5f for the first time is a significant question mark.

runners_data.name: Wild Blossom
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Good for Karl Burke with James Doyle — a strong combination who place horses well; her style is genuinely uncertain, and the redistribution to the rear of the map simply reflects limited pace data rather than a true hold-up profile, so Doyle may push her forward early.|
runners_data.comment: Wild Blossom announced herself with a dominant 10-length novice success on debut at Carlisle 30 days ago, and connections landed this very race in 2024; effective at the trip on good ground, she shapes as the one to beat from stall 7, though the draw merits watching.

runners_data.note: Non-runner; had she run she would have been the sole confirmed front-runner and her absence fundamentally changes

races.paceDynamic: With Your Song declared a non-runner, this race loses its one confirmed front-runner, leaving a field dominated almost entirely by prominent-style two-year-old fillies with no natural lead horse to fill the vacuum. The result is a pace paradox: a field packed with runners who want to race handy but with nobody willing or bred to set a true gallop from the front, meaning the early fractions on Good To Firm ground at Ascot's straight five will likely be contested and scrappy rather than smoothly run. Whoever bounces to the lead — most likely one of the higher-drawn, gate-smart types such as Senorita Bonita, Victorious, Shimmering Sun or Lover Girl — will be doing so under pressure from multiple rivals, creating a mid-race scramble that tests resolution as much as raw speed. This field holds considerably more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate, with Havana Lightning, Fast Track, Envision, Alta Regina and Armor Supreme among those most likely to be shuffled back from their natural positions; the fillies best placed to secure a clean prominent berth in stalls 1–10 are the most likely beneficiaries. The tactical verdict is clear: in a race where pace is contested from multiple angles on fast ground over a straight five, horses that can slot just off a scrappy lead — racing prominent but not fighting for the front — hold the most favourable profile, and those with the tactical versatility to find a clean position early without burning energy will have the clearest path.

races.name: Queen's Vase (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Ran creditably behind subsequent winners on her last two starts including a second on soft ground; the natural front-running/prominent tendency will be squeezed out by a field loaded with pace, meaning she is unlikely to recreate the forward berth that suits her best.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 1¼ lengths in a Listed race latest when still looking green in front, Asakir is progressive and open to more improvement; first-time cheekpieces and a more patient ride over this trip on suitable ground could see him go very close, though inexperience remains the main risk.

runners_data.name: Del Maro
runners_data.note: Consistent Charlie Appleby/William Buick runner with a win at 1m2f and placed efforts at 1m3f on good ground, stepping up in trip here; sits well within the prominent cluster and benefits from a clean expected race shape, though the class ceiling against Galiyan and Limestone is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a nose in a Listed race at Goodwood latest when fitted with cheekpieces, Del Maro arrives in cracking form from a trainer firing on all cylinders, stays well and acts on any going — the chief concern is whether he can convert that near-miss into victory.

runners_data.name: Galiyan
runners_data.note: Top-rated co-runner at OR 120 alongside Point Of Law; won a Goodwood Listed over 1m4f last time and Oisin Murphy's positive style suits prominent tracking here, with Andrew Balding's 12/66 14-day strike rate providing further confidence in timing.
runners_data.comment: Galiyan won a Chester maiden by 2¼ lengths last time out and, with a top course trainer in the saddle, the step up to 14f looks a logical next move for a horse still developing — effective at 10-12f on good ground, though this rise in grade is the one test.

runners_data.name: Limestone
runners_data.note: Five-time winner including two recent successes over 1m3f and 1m5f for Joseph O'Brien; DBM rides and the headgear flag (tongue tie) is noted — three wins in five on good ground and a staying profile that could be the most potent in the field if Galiyan is tested.
runners_data.comment: Limestone arrives on the back of three consecutive wins, most recently a Listed success at Navan over 13f, and looks a progressive sort with the right attitude — first-time headgear adds a small query, though the trip and going profile suit well.

runners_data.name: Magnetude
runners_data.note: James Owen's dual winner at 1m4f on good and standard; a natural prominent racer who will find this Ascot field too deep in pace-committed runners to travel where he wants, and his OR 81 also asks a stiff class question against Group 2 rivals.
runners_data.comment: Magnetude won a Chester handicap last time in first-time cheekpieces, retains them here, and the form figures look solid, but this is a significantly tougher assignment and, ranked last on our figures, there are serious doubts about the step up in class.

runners_data.name: Mr Colonel
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides for the Fahey yard; won over 1m2f at Leopardstown last time and has placed consistently on good ground, wearing a tongue tie throughout his career — the unknown quantity is whether his form translates to this class and distance step, but he is a genuine midfield competitor.
runners_data.comment: Wore a tongue-tie for the first time when a staying-on 6-length third in the Chester Vase last time out, running to his best over 12f — but drawn widest with a bend soon after the start adds a complication, and he has a bit to find on these terms.

runners_data.name: Point Of Law
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Gosden/Doyle send him here off a good-ground maiden win over 1m2f and the sole lead role at Ascot over 1m6f is a significant tactical gift, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder that being alone in front at this level carries its own burden.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of promise when winning a Newbury maiden last time, hitting the line well, but faces a stiff rise in class here and our figures rank it near the foot of the field — a step up to 12f on a sound surface looks the longer-term target.

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien, but recent form reads 5-7-3-5-1 and the hold-up position in a potentially moderate-tempo race is far from ideal — best trip appears shorter based on his Leopardstown Listed win over 1m and the step to 1m6f adds further doubt.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces couldn't spark a revival on handicap debut at Newbury last time, beaten four-and-a-quarter lengths, and ranked near the foot of this field on our figures — the yard has a fine record in this race but Port Of Spain looks a below-par representative, despite a top course jockey aboard.

runners_data.name: Ranga Tang
runners_data.note: A second James Owen runner; won over 1m4f last time on good ground and has placed at 1m2f, but like stablemate Magnetude is a natural prominent type forced wide of his best position by the congested pace map, and OR 83 is a steep class ask.
runners_data.comment: Showed a good attitude to get up by a short-head at Salisbury last time, and stays 12f well on today's going, but this big, gangly colt needs to improve again to be competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Ravenspire
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts over 1m4f-1m5f for Karl Burke, whose 7/46 14-day record shows the yard is ticking; she arrives after 53 days off and will need to race a little further back than is natural, yet the unexposed profile over exactly this sort of stamina test means she carries genuine each-way interest at a likely big price.
runners_data.comment: Ravenspire arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, most recently defying a penalty in taking style at Haydock, and still looked green there — suggesting more improvement is likely. The step up in trip should suit this big colt, though 53 days off and a penalty to carry are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Wareeth
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's horse won a 1m2f handicap last time and a 1m0f novice before that; pushed to the rear by the redistribution process but is fundamentally a prominent-style runner, and Tom Marquand would ideally be forward — the held-up assignment here is against instinct and the form profile looks light for Group 2 company.
runners_data.comment: Wareeth bolted up by six lengths on his latest start and rates 15lb above his official mark, making him a compelling threat here — though stepping up 4f in trip and into considerably better company are the key questions he must answer.

races.paceDynamic: Point Of Law is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival prepared to challenge for the lead, will settle into an uncontested, controlled tempo down the Ascot straight mile-and-six on Good to Firm ground — conditions that reward class and a clean trip rather than stamina attrition. Galiyan, Del Maro, Limestone and Mr Colonel all sit naturally in the prominent-to-midfield cluster behind him, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a scrappy gallop. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate: Asakir, Ravenspire, Ranga Tang, Magnetude and Wareeth are all natural prominent racers who will be unable to secure their preferred position, with Galiyan and Limestone best-placed to actually hold the prominent slots given their superior class and connections. A solo, unhurried lead at a sustainable clip over this trip on fast ground sets up the race for a horse who can either control and quicken from the front, or track two wide and deploy a decisive turn of foot in the straight — the prominent, class-laden, track-positioned profile is strongly favoured.

watchPoints.text: Point Of Law has the race entirely to himself in front — watch whether James Doyle elects to slow the fractions dramatically, which would transform this into a sprint finish and compress the field, benefiting those with the sharpest turn of foot rather than true stayers.

Galiyan and Limestone are both prominent types chasing the same tracking position directly behind Point Of Law — if they clash for the same ground turning into the straight, one or both could get a rough passage that compromises a genuine winning chance.

Port Of Spain has Ryan Moore in the saddle, who is capable of producing a horse from any position — if the pace is stronger than expected and the field does string out, his hold-up role becomes more credible and should not be completely ignored mid-race.

Ravenspire has been off for 53 days and is unbeaten but lightly raced — watch the market move for Burke's filly, as any support for an unexposed stayer at this trip on fast ground could signal strong stable confidence ahead of a potential market surprise.

races.name: Duke Of Cambridge Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies & Mares)

runners_data.name: Jancis
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has strong course form and handles Good ground (10 runs, 3W 4P on similar going); sits naturally just off the pace and Levey is likely to use that position to secure an inside rail berth early, making her a key player if a controlled tempo sets up a battle for the prominent spots.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a tongue-tie for the first time and carrying 131 lb from stall 9, Jancis arrives just 24 days after finishing fifth in a Group 2 when finishing well but finding the task beyond her — though that Dahlia form is arguably flattered, her best coming from off the pace hoping for trouble in running.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Johnston runner has slipped to a career-low OR of 102 and recorded just one win from 15 runs on similar ground; though she naturally wants to race prominently, the crowded pace map pushes her into a midfield slot she has not proved effective from, and a 46-day absence adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Arisaig shaped with plenty of promise when fourth, beaten just 2½ lengths in Listed company at Goodwood latest, and a strong pace will play to her hand — this hold-up filly closes best on fast ground and is well suited by today's conditions. The chief concern is her winless recent run of form.

runners_data.name: Blue Bolt
runners_data.note: Consistent mare who has won five of her last seven runs including two at this 8f trip on Good ground — her record in this sphere is the standout in the field; Colin Keane will aim to slot her into a prominent position and she is well-placed to dominate if that berth is secured.
runners_data.comment: Blue Bolt arrives on the back of a smooth Listed win at Goodwood, travelling well before asserting late, and her record of three wins in her last five starts underlines consistent form; a top course trainer, she's at her best on a sound surface and our rating of 136 marks her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over on this lightly-raced four-year-old with wins at 7f and 8f on Standard, but her two runs on Good ground show limited exposed form on this surface; her natural front-running style has been squeezed out of its optimal position by the crowded pace map and her chance relies on Moore manufacturing something from a more restrained role.
runners_data.comment: Finished a length second in a Group 2 latest but ranks last of 15 here and has a clear step up in class to find, making her genuinely hard to fancy despite a top course jockey booking and proven versatility on any surface.

runners_data.name: Catalina Delcarpio
runners_data.note: Paul Twomey runner brings wins at 8f and 10f, but her best efforts have come on Good to Firm-plus or Good with cut; she is a naturally forceful front-end operator who will be denied that position here, and her 38-day break is manageable, though the step back in trip from her most recent runs could sharpen her up.
runners_data.comment: Ran to her very best when landing a Listed prize last time out, and the yard is firing — but 38 days off and a rating of 104 leave her with ground to make up on official marks, even if she's likely to finish strongly over this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Cathedral
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's four-year-old has placed twice in six attempts at this trip and excels when close to the pace with a strong gallop in front of her; David Egan should be able to track the leaders and her ability to handle a genuine test at 8f on Good ground makes her one of the more straightforward prominent types in the field.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and versatile, Cathedral was a close second in a Newmarket Group 2 last time despite being caught up in a fierce pace, and that effort reads well for this. Winless in her last five starts, she'll need to convert that form into a clear success here.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett filly who has produced her best work over 7f on Good or Soft, and her lone win came over that shorter trip; she is a front-end type by nature but is pushed back by the congested pace map, and stepping up to 8f here on quicker ground than her comfort zone is a double ask.
runners_data.comment: Returned from 39 days off to finish seventh at Lingfield last time, likely needing that run, but back-to-back modest efforts before that single win make this a tough sell, and ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, there's little to draw you in.

runners_data.name: Falakeyah
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows runner has two wins over 8f-10f including on Standard, but her two runs at this level on Good ground have seen her beaten; she wants to be prominent but the crowded pace configuration means she will be forced to settle further back than ideal, which tempers the strength of her claims here.
runners_data.comment: Showed her class when winning over today's trip and going, but the Newmarket run 45 days ago — where she raced too freely and was well held at Group 2 level — raises questions about whether she can translate her undoubted ability into a consistent performance.

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse and the only true closer in this field — Soumillon will drop her out and produce a sustained late run, and her two wins on Good at this trip show she is in good order; she is the natural beneficiary if the pace collapses late, and Francophone's form string shows consistency under a patient ride.
runners_data.comment: Held up and needing plenty to go right, Francophone was beaten four lengths in a Group 2 last time and ranks 11th of 15 on our figures — the form profile and rating gap make it hard to fancy, though course-and-distance experience on this going at least counts for something.

runners_data.name: Friendly Soul
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's five-year-old is the race's lone pace-setter and has won her last three in a row; she is a confirmed front-runner who will dictate, and while her most recent runs have come over 10f and on softer ground, she has a 1m Good win in her history, and Murphy is the key booking here — though her STYLE_FIT flag reflects she carries some tactical risk if caught.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time only after a false step when still going well, and with the yard having won this race in each of the last two years, Friendly Soul arrives with serious claims on the back of three wins in her last five starts — the only question is how much edge she retains after missing most of 2025.

runners_data.name: Godspeed
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this C&Y Lerner-trained four-year-old who has placed but never won at this trip on Good, earning OR 109 from a second at 7f soft last time; she races prominently and is likely to be competitive for the real positions behind the leader, but her absent win record on Good ground keeps her one step behind the principals.
runners_data.comment: Ran to Listed-level form when going down by a short-neck at Longchamp latest, and Group 1 experience demands respect, but 55 days off the track and a stall-12 draw are factors to weigh against a field in which he rates just seventh on our figures.

runners_data.name: Kon Tiki
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's four-year-old has three wins in five career starts including at 8f on Good, showing genuine ability; though naturally a prominent runner, she has been mapped to the rear due to an unusually pace-light hold-up section — her real chance is if Billy Loughnane can manoeuvre her forward early despite the style mismatch implied by her mapped position.
runners_data.comment: Shown she handles the trip and conditions, and her Goodwood Listed placing last time — beaten just three-quarters of a length when worn down late — reads well; 46 days between runs and 128 lb are the checks, but she's capable of making the frame again.

runners_data.name: Noche Clasica
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell runner with three wins including at 8f on Good, but she has dropped from 105 OR to 98 and her latest runs at Group level have seen her placed and unplaced; she wants to be prominent but is squeezed back in the pace map, and the improvement required to feature at Group 2 level from her current form figures is significant.
runners_data.comment: Noche Clasica brings a progressive profile — three wins in its last five starts — and acts on today's conditions, but this drop in trip may blunt its edge after looking suited by 10f when a close fourth at Listed level last time.

runners_data.name: Shes Perfect
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' four-year-old wore a hood for the first time last time out and ran only 11 days ago — the short turnaround is notable; she has placed consistently but her form at 8f and her best ground is Soft, and coming back for a Group 2 quickly on Good to Firm is a combination of pressures that make her a difficult case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and struggling to find 2025 form, Shes Perfect boiled over before her latest outing and raced too freely when well held; first-time cheekpieces are a mild interest, but she remains hard to fancy at the foot of the rankings.

runners_data.name: Snellen
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old has an exceptional record on similar going — all 15 runs on Good-type ground, four wins nine places; she is naturally front-running but gets crowded out of that position here, and Mark Zahra will need to work quietly from an enforced midfield role, which is a genuine constraint on her ability to reproduce her best form.
runners_data.comment: Ran well fresh when a close third at Group 3 level last time, and handles today's trip and ground, but ranked near the foot of our assessments and likely needs to find more than that form suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Friendly Soul is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy aboard, will stride on from the gates and attempt to control this mile at a measured, honest pace on Good to Firm ground. The field is stacked with prominent-racing types — Snellen, Carolina Jetstream, Catalina Delcarpio, Falakeyah, Dash Of Azure and others all want to race close to the pace but cannot all occupy those berths — meaning several will be shuffled back into an unnatural midfield position and their form profiles must be discounted accordingly. Jancis, Blue Bolt, Cathedral and Godspeed are the genuine prominent horses most likely to actually sit just behind Friendly Soul and secure the positions behind the leader. The resulting shape — a controlled tempo set by one horse with a cluster of true prominents jostling just off it — strongly favours horses who can travel fluidly in the first five and deploy a sustained finish from a genuine position, rather than closers forced wide from the rear, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the sweet spot in this race.

watchPoints.text: Friendly Soul must be monitored closely from the stalls — if she misses the break or is harassed in the first two furlongs by Carolina Jetstream or Snellen angling for position, the entire pace structure collapses and a more chaotic shape unfolds.

Blue Bolt's stall draw and early positioning are critical — she has dominated at this level and trip, but with six or more horses also wanting the prominent spots, any traffic or crowding in the first quarter-mile could cost her the clean passage her form demands.

Francophone is the only genuine hold-up runner and Soumillon will ride her cold — watch whether the pace is truly strong enough to bring her into contention, because if Friendly Soul dawdles, the closer's finish will not reach the principals.

Several redistributed prominents — notably Snellen, Catalina Delcarpio and Falakeyah — will likely be squeezed wider and further back than ideal in the opening furlong; watch for traffic incidents or horses getting badly outpaced early as they are forced out of their natural positions.

Shes Perfect runs back just 11 days after her last start and is fitted with headgear — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for signs of freshness or a keyed-up temperament, as a repeat of any quirky behaviour could undermine her chance before the race has properly developed.

races.name: Prince Of Wales's Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almaqam
runners_data.note: Won a Group 2 at Goodwood last time on Good ground and arrives in strong form, but his natural prominent style is compromised here — there are simply too many forward-going rivals and he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, reducing his chance in the dominant shape.
runners_data.comment: Almaqam arrives fresh from a convincing 2-length Tattersalls Gold Cup victory at the Curragh, and with course-and-distance form to call upon and strong claims as a progressive five-year-old, he's a serious threat from stall 1 under 128lb — fast ground the one factor to watch.

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: Shaped with headgear (p) and has a modest recent form string (390-64) over shorter, making the step up to 1m2f and this elite company a significant ask; a genuine hold-up operator who needs a truly run race to maximise his late effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but shaped with promise when fourth in the Lockinge latest, and the first-time cheekpieces stay on here; held up over a suited trip, though fast ground would be preferred and this looks a stiff ask regardless.

runners_data.name: Daryz
runners_data.note: On a remarkable three-race winning streak including a Group 1 victory, he is a proper prominent performer who should settle in Ombudsman's slipstream for Barzalona; his Good-to-Firm form is limited (3 runs at similar going) but his class is evident and the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Daryz arrives in career-best form after a facile 3½-length Group 1 success at Longchamp last time, and as the reigning Arc winner has the class to dominate again — the sole concern is whether the going proves quick enough to see the best of him.

runners_data.name: Devil's Advocate
runners_data.note: Arrives fresh after 54 days off for the Gosden stable, who are in good 14-day form (7/24); a hold-up operator with zero wins or places on Good ground at 10f in his history, which is an honest concern, and he needs the pace to collapse for his closing run to count.
runners_data.comment: Held up as a pacemaker for a stablemate, Devil's Advocate is tough to fancy in his own right — pulled 18 lengths clear latest on ground probably too fast, and the first-time headgear does little to shorten the odds at the bottom of the market, even if the yard won this last year.

runners_data.name: Mississippi River
runners_data.note: Last seen finishing tailed-off in a Group race and his form reads 51-570, yet his natural style is prominent — one of three such types pushed off the front by this field's composition, making him a high-risk proposition who must overcome positional compromise as well as a form dip.
runners_data.comment: Mississippi River finished out of the frame most recently after being deployed as a pacemaker at Group 1 level, and returns here likely in a similar role — bottom of our rankings among eight runners, the first-time blinkers do little to change that outlook despite proven course-and-distance form.

runners_data.name: Ombudsman
runners_data.note: The in-form confirmed pace-setter who arrives off a 20-day break, wins regularly on Good ground (6W from 9 similar-going runs), and has William Buick to engineer a clean lead; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects the density of the prominent brigade but he is the one most likely to actually secure it.
runners_data.comment: Ombudsman won this race 12 months ago and backed it up with a Brigadier Gerard Stakes success last time, making him the obvious one to beat on a going that suits; the yard is in form and a 20-day turnaround looks ideal, though a neck margin last time hints he's not foot-perfect.

runners_data.name: Minnie Hauk
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners a filly with four wins from 10 starts and strong course-relevant form at 10-12f; she is a legitimate prominent type who should get a clean run in second or third and her finishing record at the trip suggests she is ideally set up for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Minnie Hauk, the 2025 Oaks winner effective over this trip and proven on the going, arrives 24 days fresh and shaped as a leading danger at 125lb from stall 5 — though she must bounce back after a puzzling 9-length defeat last time out.

runners_data.name: See The Fire
runners_data.note: Two wins on the bounce coming into this, both on Good ground at 10f, which is squarely on trend — but his prominent tendency is squeezed by the pack, and Oisin Murphy will likely find him racing further back than he wants, blunting the momentum he carried into this race.
runners_data.comment: Landed the Middleton Fillies' Stakes (Group 2) at York last time and clearly thrives at the course, but was third here 12 months ago and needs to find more to go one better; in-form, trainer excels here, though our rating suggests she's just held on form assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Ombudsman is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with William Buick aboard, will stride into the lead from the off and dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Ascot. The pace he sets will be honest but measured — not a sprint, not a crawl — creating a classic mid-tempo Group 1 shape where the race is won in the final two furlongs rather than run out from the front. Daryz and Minnie Hauk are the genuine prominent horses likely to sit just off Ombudsman's shoulder, with the field bunching into a compact formation; runners with a high cruising speed and the ability to quicken from just off the pace are therefore best placed to exploit the shape. This field holds more prominent-minded types than can all secure their natural position — Almaqam, See The Fire, and Mississippi River are all naturally prominent but at least one or two will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, making their tasks materially harder. The race shape strongly favours horses that can sit second or third and produce a clean, sustained pick-up in the straight — a profile that rewards class and acceleration over raw stamina or a late-closing kick.

watchPoints.text: Ombudsman's early lead bid is the race's central tactical hinge — if he jumps cleanly and settles in front uncontested by the first furlong, the race shape crystallises immediately in favour of the sit-and-quicken profile.

Almaqam, See The Fire, and Mississippi River are all natural prominent runners who cannot all occupy that ground — watch the first two furlongs for positional friction, potential checking, and energy burned before the race properly begins.

Devil's Advocate's 54-day absence is notable for the Gosden yard; watch his market movement on the day and how sharply he moves through his gears early as an indicator of whether the freshness is an asset or a concern.

Dancing Gemini steps into Group 1 company off a string of defeats over 8f — monitor whether Roger Teal has targeted this trip deliberately as a stamina-based angle, or whether this is a speculative entry at a higher level than his form warrants.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for the 4:20, and several runners including Daryz and Mississippi River have limited exposure at this precise going variant — horses with the most proven records on Good to Firm (Ombudsman, Minnie Hauk) carry an additional ground-form edge.

races.name: Royal Hunt Cup (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Holloway Boy
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner with excellent sim-going figures (12/15 on good); Jack Nicholls claims 5lb, which may matter in a handicap, and 47 days off is not a concern for K R Burke — but his official style tag here reflects that with no pressure he controls this.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and placing regularly in recent starts, Holloway Boy sweats up but has shown he handles that, finishing second in a Listed race here latest; winless in his last five, though, and a mark of 112 makes life tough back in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Skukuza
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon booked is a significant positive for a yard in form; visor headgear worn, recent form is patchy (5th, 6th, 6th) and soft-ground efforts outnumber good-ground wins, so conditions here are a mild query despite the respectable sim-going figures.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and disappointing when beaten seven lengths at Epsom last time after racing too freely, Skukuza dons a visor for the first time from stall 17 — that headgear switch is the main hook, though a run of declining figures suggests form remains a concern.

runners_data.name: Linwood
runners_data.note: Won last two outings (both on good ground at 8f), Jamie Spencer is an ideal partner for this trip and Jamie Hannon has 9 winners from 44 runners in the 14-day window — this horse arrives in the strongest form of the prominent group and conditions suit exactly.
runners_data.comment: Successive wins — including a ¾-length Newbury Spring Cup success off a lower mark — mark Linwood as a major player returning fresh to a distance and going that suits; the new, higher handicap mark is the main hurdle to clear.

runners_data.name: No Retreat
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground over 7-8f and finished second behind a subsequent winner here; 123 days off is the main concern but George Scott has him fresh and Billy Loughnane rides with confidence — a horse that often produces a peak effort first time out.
runners_data.comment: Ran creditably in Listed company last time but that was 123 days ago, and returning from a break to tackle a competitive handicap off 135 lb makes this a tough ask — consistent over today's trip and going, yet sits well down the rankings on our figures.

runners_data.name: Excellent Believe
runners_data.note: Back-to-back placed efforts (2nd, 3rd) at 8f on good ground for Jack Channon; the 7lb claimer Toby Moore adds appeal but also risk in a 30-runner handicap, and the horse has not won on good ground — placed regularly but hard to fancy at the top.
runners_data.comment: Placed in Listed company last time despite late interference, Excellent Believe has the class to compete here, though a career-high 134lb — 11lb above last handicap mark — makes things tough; acts on the going and has form over today's distance.

runners_data.name: Archivist
runners_data.note: James McDonald is a strong booking and this horse won its last two at 8f on good ground; lightly raced at this trip with a hood worn (hg:h), and 96 days off could mean he arrives fresh and cherry-ripe — a horse with genuine upside in this company.
runners_data.comment: Archivist landed a Meydan handicap by 2¼ lengths off this very mark last time out and is proven over today's trip and conditions, making it the one to beat here despite the 96-day absence and first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going record (13/15 on good/similar) for David O'Meara, who has a prolific 14-day record; Tudhope fits this track well and a recent second at 8f on good ground means the horse arrives in fair order, though winning form has been elusive lately.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck at York last time off a 2lb lower mark, Cerulean Bay arrives in cracking heart but faces a stiffer task from 133lb here; consistent in top handicaps and versatile on ground, though fortune in running from stall 22 will matter.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: Muir & Grassick yard is cold (0 from 12 in 14 days) and this horse's recent form has been moderate (18th, 4th); pairs well with good ground but recent disappointing efforts make it hard to enthuse, despite a Lewis Edmunds partner.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who travelled well before fading late at Newbury off a 1lb lower mark, suggesting stamina may be stretched; winless in his last five starts and now 7lb higher than 12 months ago, with stall 32 to factor in from 132lb.

runners_data.name: Henlein
runners_data.note: Poor recent form — 7th, 15th in last two runs over shorter trips than ideal; Kevin Stott keeps the ride but Kevin Ryan's 14-day numbers are modest and the step back to 8f after two poor efforts at 7f doesn't inspire confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last four starts and ranked well down our assessments, Henlein shaped with some promise on British debut at Haydock last time off a 1lb higher mark, though a 53-day break and declining recent form make it hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Thunder Run
runners_data.note: Dist-drop to 8f from 10f+ in recent starts is notable — has placed third and second over 10f on good but yet to convince at a mile; Clifford Lee takes the mount for K R Burke who is in form, but the horse's profile fits slightly longer distances.
runners_data.comment: Thunder Run shaped well at York last time, going down by a length off a 3lb lower mark than today's, and handles this trip and going — but winless in his last five starts and there are doubts about whether he truly has the pace for a mile.

runners_data.name: Chibitty
runners_data.note: 117 days off is the standout flag here; placed at 8f and 9f on soft/heavy but poor sim-going record on good (3/7), Sean Levey rides but the Simcock yard has been quiet and a long absence on possibly unsuitable ground is a double concern.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths in a handicap last time and ranked bottom of 30 on our figures, Chibitty faces an uphill task from stall 25 carrying 131lb off a stiff mark, and 117 days off the track adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Urban Lion
runners_data.note: Won most recently on soft over 8f and beaten a long way on good ground (24th) — going conditions are a legitimate worry; Edward Greatrex rides, Jack Channon yard, but the sim-going record (9/14 on good) is mixed and recent efforts at this trip have been poor.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 30 lengths into 24th on latest start off the same mark he carries today, Urban Lion needs a significant bounce-back on this return from 60 days off, and ranking 22nd of 30 on our figures makes it hard to fancy despite proven course, distance, and going credentials.

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature — three wins from six at 8f on good ground and a very high style-fit score confirm that; Colin Keane is a top booking for Stephen Thorne, but the crowded prominent group means this horse is extremely unlikely to get its natural race-shape and the redistribution tag is the key factor to note.
runners_data.comment: Blows hot and cold in recent starts and now 9lb higher than when landing that Naas handicap, making the current mark tough to overcome — though a significant jockey booking and proven effectiveness over today's trip are genuine points in its favour.

runners_data.name: Checkandchallenge
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a tongue-tie (hg:p), winning form is absent (0 wins in recent five); Rossa Ryan for William Knight who is modest in 14-day numbers, and a horse that repeatedly finishes mid-pack in this type of race — better ground doesn't appear to unlock a new gear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and seemingly in decline, Checkandchallenge's mark looks stiff, though first-time headgear and a career-best effort somewhat masked by a four-length Newbury defeat last time offer mild encouragement for this 8-10f performer who handles any ground.

runners_data.name: Fifth Column
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner pushed back by the crowded map — William Buick is an elite booking for Gosden and the horse has three wins in its last 14 runs on good ground; if Buick can manoeuvre closer to the pace than mapped, its chance improves markedly from the shown position.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when beaten half a length at Newmarket last time off a 1lb lower mark, and first-time headgear could sharpen things up for a trainer firing at 29%; however, 46 days off and a rise in the weights are the counterweights to consider.

runners_data.name: La Botte
runners_data.note: Three wins at 8f but recent form is poor (8th, 7th, 14th) with none on genuinely good ground working in its favour (only 1 placed from 8 sim-going); Mark Zahra rides for Harry Eustace and the horse would need to recapture form last seen last year — tough ask in this company from a forced midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Britannia runner-up who acts on today's trip and surface, and with a trainer in form there's plenty to work with — yet to score in recent starts, and closing that gap to the top flight remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: A genuinely high-quality prominent runner displaced into midfield by the crowded map — Oisin Murphy's booking is significant and this horse has won twice at 8f on good ground in its last three starts; if Murphy can slot into a forward position early, this horse's chance is better than its mapped position implies.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Epsom 12 days ago, hitting the line well off a 5lb lower mark than today's, and handles this course, distance and going well — though that rise in the weights and a tendency to race keenly are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Erzindjan
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on board is always noteworthy, and this horse did win last time out over 9f on good ground; an 8-year-old whose sim-going record (14/15) is outstanding, but the hold-up style in a field that may not truly run fast is a structural problem — Moore's positional genius is the key variable.
runners_data.comment: Landed the Suffolk Stakes Handicap at Newmarket last time out by a short head, though that came off a 2lb lower mark and faces a stiffer task here from stall 24 carrying 129lb; a big run remains feasible on ground he handles.

runners_data.name: One Smack Mac
runners_data.note: 277 days off is the longest absence in the field — Saffie Osborne for Jamie Osborne, but a horse returning from near a year away with moderate recent form at distances shorter than this mile; very hard to recommend at a competitive handicap mark on a first run back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and absent for 277 days, One Smack Mac needs a bounce back on what appears to be a stable debut — a first-time hood at least offers some intrigue, but this outsider asks plenty of faith after a string of below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Godwinson
runners_data.note: Another natural front-runner remapped into midfield — George Bass is an inexperienced rider for a Jack Channon yard that is quiet in the 14-day data; the horse's last win came on standard/artificial and good-ground record (5 from 15) is poor, so even if it gets its preferred position the form needs a significant bounce.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive unplaced runs, including a thumping 8½-length defeat last time, make Godwinson hard to fancy, and fast ground adds a further concern for a horse who handles soft and AW surfaces best.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (0/0 in last two, off 10/19 on similar going) with a weak sim-going record (3/15); Cieren Fallon for Ian Williams who has not had a winner in 41 runners over 14 days — this horse is hard to back with any conviction on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and needing more off a mark of 100, Ozat's recent record — including a well-beaten Epsom handicap effort 12 days ago — makes it hard to fancy, especially with a struggling trainer. Acts on today's ground and distance, at least.

runners_data.name: Blue Rc
runners_data.note: Twice placed on standard going (synthetic) at 8f but good-ground record is mixed (5/11 sim-going); Hector Crouch for James Tate who has reasonable 14-day numbers, and the horse won twice at 8f on standard — its true-prominent nature mapped to midfield means it will need to travel well early for Crouch to find a gap.
runners_data.comment: Blue Rc arrives on the back of a below-par Newbury handicap defeat — beaten six lengths — after two encouraging runner-up efforts, so a bounce-back is required; acts on today's distance and going, and that prior consistency suggests the ability is there if returning to form.

runners_data.name: War Socks
runners_data.note: Recent placed efforts at 8-10f on good ground suggest solid ability; David Egan for Niels Petersen whose 14-day data is thin — a genuine prominent horse assigned a midfield slot means Egan will face a positioning challenge in this big field from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Improved by four lengths winning a Bro Park handicap off this mark last time, but as a Scandinavian raider ranked 25th of 30 on our figures, War Socks faces a stiff ask stepping into this company from stall 21 carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Shout
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on soft and has placed on good; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a useful allowance but the horse was 9th in its most recent run and the Crisford yard's 14-day numbers are modest — a natural prominent type that cannot get its position in this race.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when beaten two lengths off this mark at York last time, but remains 8lb above the rating at which it last won — a consistent profile that promises more placed efforts than victories right now.

runners_data.name: Classic
runners_data.note: Two wins at 8f on good and second most recently — strong form claims for a Pat Dobbs/Richard Hannon combination who are both very active in the Ascot handicap sphere; the redistribution to midfield from a natural prominent slot is the single biggest obstacle to this horse fulfilling its form potential.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a neck win in a handicap at Newbury last time off a 4lb lower mark than today, and handles today's trip and surface well — though up in the weights now and a wide draw to contend with from stall 19.

runners_data.name: Swing Vote
runners_data.note: 109 days off and a poor recent form string (5th, 8th, 6th, 7th) including a tongue-tie flag; Silvestre De Sousa for Crisford, but the horse's track record (three wins on good over a mile) is the only encouraging note — it is hard to catch these after
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and below best when well beaten on its latest outing, Swing Vote returns after a 109-day absence in first-time headgear carrying 127lb from stall 27 — a combination of factors that make this a difficult one to fancy, despite proven effectiveness at this trip on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Indalo
runners_data.comment: Ran to a neck defeat off 3lb lower at Newbury last time and remains progressive in 2025, but steps up in weight from stall 8 wearing first-time headgear — with course-and-distance form on its side and connections landing this race last year, there's plenty to like.

runners_data.name: Rogue Diplomat
runners_data.comment: Ran creditably in Listed company last time but steps back into a competitive handicap from stall 33 carrying 126 lb, and ranked 23 of 30 on our figures — hard to fancy at likely odds, though course-and-distance form and versatility on any going offer some consolation.

runners_data.name: Scoville
runners_data.comment: Scoville has the form figures to be a leading player here — effective at a mile on sound ground, a top jockey back in the plate and a trainer firing at 37% — but first-time cheekpieces suggest a settling issue, and if he pulls hard again, that's the main danger to his chance.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.comment: Showed smart form when winning in recent starts and acts on this trip and going, but has disappointed in his last four runs including a poor effort at Newbury last time, so needs to rediscover that earlier spark from stall 3 in this large field.

races.paceDynamic: Holloway Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 30-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival likely to press him hard — with Mister Winston, La Botte, Jagged Edge, War Socks, Classic and multiple other natural prominent types unable to secure their preferred position in such a congested field, Holloway Boy is set to control this from the front at a comfortable, sustainable gallop. That scenario is highly likely to produce a moderate pace through the middle section of the straight mile, with the tempo picking up only in the final quarter-mile — a shape that compresses the field and narrows the sectional gap between front and back. With so many genuine front-runners redistributed into midfield against their will, the contest is likely to resemble a tactical crawl-then-sprint, benefiting horses that can travel fluently in a prominent-to-midfield position and accelerate off a slow pace rather than those who need the race truly run to suit them from the rear. The dominant profile to side with here is the horse that secures a prominent position just off Holloway Boy's shoulder and produces a sharp turn of foot on the good-to-firm ground — true hold-up types are structurally disadvantaged in a 30-runner field with limited pace.
