races.name: Kensington Palace Stakes (Fillies' Handicap)

runners_data.name: Stateira
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner ridden by James Doyle for Andrew Balding (8/64 in 14 days); won twice over this 8f trip on similar going, and with no rival willing to press her the tempo is entirely hers to dictate — STYLE_FIT note is secondary here as she is actually being placed in her natural prominent/lead role in this field context.
runners_data.comment: Stateira's hat-trick of recent wins and a cracking third in a Group 2 last time demonstrate she's in red-hot form, and with a trainer who won this race last year and handles this trip well, she's a serious contender — the 138lb burden is the one thing to overcome.

runners_data.name: Sand Gazelle
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over for Gosden and the hold-up style suits a patient ride in a big field; steps back from 9-10f and the drop to 1m is worth watching, though she won over 10f on Good and her closing form is consistent.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers applied for the first time after cheekpieces failed to spark a revival — beaten 10 lengths at Listed level last time and out of sorts all season, though a winner in recent starts and proven over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Muddy Mooy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Charlie Pike dropping slightly in trip; trainer without a winner in 14 days and 54 days off the track — needs to bounce back to her 3/2 form in soft/good conditions, which she has not reproduced on faster ground.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held in a Group 3 last time and winless in its last five starts, Muddy Mooy also faces a ground concern here and returns after 54 days off — hard to fancy at the head of the weights from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer filly who has won twice at 8f on Good, races prominently and has a genuine chance if she repeats her 4/8f FIR run on similar conditions; cheekpieces worn and Billy Loughnane takes the ride as she tries to build on a five-race run where she has hit the board frequently.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths at Haydock last time in Listed company where the trip may have stretched her, Cheshire Dancer looks more at home back at a mile on a sound surface, though she's been out of sorts this season and first-time headgear is needed to spark a revival from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Gaga Girl
runners_data.note: Gerald Mosse-trained filly with a tongue-tie who finished 2nd twice at 8f on Heathcote and Sandown — pattern of competitive placed form, and Soumillon's experience in big fields is a clear positive; promoted to Ascot 1m for the first time.
runners_data.comment: Gaga Girl shaped well on her latest Listed outing and acts on the going, but others look stronger on these terms, and the first-time headgear at 130lb from stall 24 adds unknowns for a filly best around a mile.

runners_data.name: American Gal
runners_data.note: Ed Walker filly who was 2nd at 8f on Good but has run nine times without a win on similar ground in recent starts — prominent racer who may find this field very competitive with an OR of 97.
runners_data.comment: American Gal has the course-distance-going profile to be involved here, effective across a range of conditions and trips, but she's winless in her last five and has yet to hit her stride this season — a stall 5 draw, 130 lb, and patchy recent figures suggest mid-division at best.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton hold-up filly who ran just 11 days ago; placed form cluster of 4/5/5 in similar races and stays 8f on Good, but the quick turnaround and her deeper hold-up style may leave her exposed in a race not guaranteed to truly run hot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but running with credit — that fourth in the Princess Elizabeth at Epsom franks the form, and she clearly handles today's trip and conditions. The 128 lb burden from stall 11 is the main query against a return to peak.

runners_data.name: Radiant Beauty
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over for the James Owen filly who won this trip and course combination (1/8f/GOO in her history); prominent racer with two wins at 8f on Good and OR=93 has her well-handicapped if she replicates her best — Moore's booking is the standout jockey signal in this field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a fillies' handicap by 2½ lengths off a 6lb lower mark last time out, but now racing off a revised mark from stall 14, and while effective at today's trip on a sound surface, the higher weight could offset that course form; Ryan Moore's booking keeps her firmly in the picture.

runners_data.name: Rhapsody
runners_data.note: William Haggas hold-up filly returning from 248 days off, which is a significant concern; won at 9f on Good and placed at 8f, and she has the class, but getting fit over Ascot 1m first time back is a tall ask even for this yard.
runners_data.comment: Rhapsody shaped with real promise when third in a Listed race on latest outing, and with the trainer in cracking form and more to offer over today's trip, the 248-day absence is the only query about a filly who looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Alobayyah
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides this Haggas prominent type who placed 3rd at 8f on Good — stepping into softer ground form in her history but this is faster, and one placed effort from four tries on Good ground is underwhelming.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form on handicap debut over this trip last time out, beaten just three lengths off a 1lb lower mark, and with a trainer firing at 37% in the last fortnight, Alobayyah looks the chief danger here; the main concern is a return to last season's lesser form.

runners_data.name: Miss Nightfall
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe filly stepping up from 7f on Good to 8f at Ascot; her best form was on Good going but the three wins on her record came at 6-7f — the extra furlong here is an open question at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and a bit below form on her return to turf at Yarmouth last time, Miss Nightfall is off an easing mark but likely needs more having probably flattered in a Group contest; effective at this trip and acts on any ground, though a sound surface may suit best.

runners_data.name: Zgharta
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's second string (Oisin Murphy) who has run six times without a win since her sole success at 8f on Good; only one placed finish in the last five runs and the form trail has been flat.
runners_data.comment: Zgharta's trainer took this race last year and the horse itself ran well at this meeting twelve months ago, making the stable combination a serious threat; however, winless in its last five starts and beaten seven lengths for pace last time out, it must find significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Seren Star
runners_data.note: Haggas filly with a tongue-tie who has won twice over 8-9f on Good ground; ran 3rd on 31 days' rest which is good prep, and Harry Davies rides — her consistent winning profile at this trip makes her a genuine pace tracker to respect.
runners_data.comment: Seren Star is an outsider on our figures, ranked well down the field, and the unplaced effort sandwiched between recent wins adds to the inconsistency. The tongue-tie applied first time and a trainer firing at 28% offer the most compelling reasons to stay interested.

runners_data.name: Crystal Flyer
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam hold-up filly whose best distances have been 9-13f — this 8f Ascot trip is the shortest she has raced recently, the form at this distance is absent, and a headgear note (hood) suggests a horse that needs managing.
runners_data.comment: Hood on for the first time after another below-par Hamilton spin 31 days ago, Crystal Flyer's winless run continues to mount — yet the versatile stayer acts on this going and distance, giving this draw-two runner a plausible each-way profile if the headgear sparks a response.

runners_data.name: Oolong Poobong
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell filly who won at 7f on Good and was 2nd at 7f — she is a natural front-running/prominent type wearing a tongue-tie, but the crowded pace scenario forces her into a midfield role that does not suit her racing pattern; style-fit concerns are real.
runners_data.comment: Ran creditably at Thirsk last time and is proven at today's trip and going, but the tongue-tie worn again may not unlock enough improvement off a mark that looks beyond reach for now — capable of filling a place rather than winning.

runners_data.name: Rumba Numba
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly won most recently at 8f on Good (12 days ago) and previously won on Stanwick going — she races naturally up with the pace and is arguably the most dangerous of the redirected prominent horses, but sharing space with multiple rivals who also want to race forward will cost her ground.
runners_data.comment: Showed a good attitude to land a handicap by a neck at Doncaster 12 days ago, and should handle the step up in weight comfortably, though slipping back to sixth in the run before is a minor caution worth noting.

runners_data.name: All Moonshine
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding three-time winner whose entire form profile reads as a prominent/front-running type — all four career runs have produced front-rank finishes, but she has been absent 126 days and races on going faster than her soft-biased form base; being shunted into midfield further complicates her reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the spin, most recently quickening clear by 2½l in a Kempton handicap off a 7lb lower mark than today, and a trainer who won this race last year fires in a strong 32% strike-rate; the 126-day absence and a 17lb rise in the weights are the obvious checks.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison hold-up filly with cheekpieces who was 2nd at 8f on Good in her most recent win — the placed form is consistent and she handles this trip, but her wider draws and hold-up style at Ascot leave her dependent on a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Ran to best when beaten a length at Thirsk 17 days ago and handles today's trip and going well, while first-time cheekpieces could sharpen the response — though winless in recent starts and a trainer in the depths of a losing run are real concerns.

runners_data.name: Unassuming
runners_data.note: George Boughey's six-year-old with a tongue-tie has four times run on Stanwick without being able to transfer that form onto Good ground at other tracks; naturally a prominent type, she is one of several redirected into midfield, and her age and recent form (45059) do not inspire confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and never competitive when well beaten at Lingfield 75 days ago, Unassuming faces an uphill task with a trainer firing at just 5% — though the first-time headgear, suitable trip and going, and a lightly encouraging earlier run offer slim crumbs of hope.

runners_data.name: Song N Dance
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne rides this S Woods filly who has excellent front-running form (211-22, two wins at 8f); she genuinely wants to race prominently but the deeply congested early pace means she may have to settle against her instincts — form on Good at 8f is strong if she gets her position.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who ran to form when beaten 2½ lengths off a 1lb lower mark last time, but steps into notably more competitive company here and our figures rank her well down the field, making it hard to fancy at likely odds from stall 19.

runners_data.name: Callianassa
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison filly whose sole win came at 8f on Stanwick and whose recent form (5/7/6) on Good ground is modest; redirected from her natural prominent style into the midfield, and the trainer has not won in 15 days.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at Chester last time and below her best form, Callianassa has posted back-to-back disappointing efforts since her last win and needs considerably more here, ranked 20 of 25 on our figures — course-and-distance form and proven going versatility offer some comfort.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old flagged as unknown style — only two runs on soft ground, 330 days off the track, and Luke Morris takes over; the profile is a complete unknown quantity in a competitive 25-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: Faces a stiff task returning from a 330-day absence, dropping in trip on fast ground that doesn't suit — conditions look against her on both counts. The Dieppe win last time out showed she can deliver, but ranked 24 of 25 on our figures, she's hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Quamby
runners_data.note: David Simcock hold-up filly who has been consistent without winning, placing four times in the last five over 8-10f on Good/Stanwick; Nicola Currie rides and the closing profile could be rewarded if the race sets up with enough pace — one of the more authentic hold-up horses in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and too keen to land a blow when fourth at Lingfield 18 days ago, Quamby does handle this trip and surface from stall 23 on 114 lb, though the overall profile suggests it faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Lady Mariko
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha filly who won at 6f on Stanwick and placed at 7f — this 8f Ascot trip is a stretch beyond her winning distance, and despite being a naturally prominent racer she is remapped into midfield with a style-fit concern that compounds the trip question.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back sixths bracket a spell of mixed form, and carrying 114 lb from stall 4, Lady Mariko looks to need more than a 1 lb drop in the weights to reverse fortunes, despite the step back to a suitable trip and proven ability to handle this going.

runners_data.name: Renesmee
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's six-year-old has placed form at 8f on Stanwick but her most recent run at 12f hints at her current preference for staying trips; raced 12 days ago in good preparation, but being a natural prominent type pushed into the midfield on a trip that may be too sharp makes her a marginal proposition.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and didn't get home last time at Goodwood, beaten eight lengths — the first-time hood and stall one offer slim angles, but this is hard to fancy against stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Stateira is the sole confirmed front-runner and, as the only genuine pace-setter in a 25-runner field, she will stride into the lead from the off and control the tempo entirely on her own terms on Good to Firm ground. With no rival capable of pressing her naturally — Cheshire Dancer, Muddy Mooy and Gaga Girl will track from prominent positions but are not true lead horses — Stateira sets a measured, sustainable gallop that is unlikely to produce a false or searching pace. The field holds significantly more prominent types than the race shape can absorb: Rumba Numba, Oolong Poobong, All Moonshine, Song N Dance, Callianassa, Lady Mariko, Renesmee and Unassuming are all genuine prominent racers who will be squeezed into midfield roles against their natural instincts, with Rumba Numba (recent course winner, Roger Varian) and Song N Dance (consistent front-runner profile, form 211-22) most likely to push forward and claim the nearest ground to Stateira. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, single-pace gallop at Ascot over one mile on fast ground overwhelmingly suits horses who can race prominently or just off the pace in the first five, track into the straight with cover, and finish with a sustained late effort — true hold-up horses starting from a compromised rearward position will face an uphill task if the pace does not truly collapse late.

runners_data.name: A Bear Affair
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's hold-up juvenile showed genuine ability finishing 7th, 3rd and winning on Good over 5f — steps up to 6f here and needs the pace to be strong enough to produce a late run from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten six lengths in a Listed contest last time but was in good form before that, and there's still improvement to come over today's trip and conditions — the question is whether this class level stretches a progressive type on a comeback run.

runners_data.name: Agitator
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole runner won impressively first time on Good over 6f at Ascot before a disappointing reappearance — genuinely prominent by nature but likely shuffled into midfield by the field's pace depth, so judge accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Broke maiden at Windsor last time out but faces a significant step up in grade here, and sits well down the rankings on our figures; the one firm positive is proven effectiveness at today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's colt won over 7f Good before a 5th over 6f Good — a natural pace-positional horse whose instinct is to race prominently, though the congested middle of the field is where he'll likely end up in this big field.|
runners_data.comment: Took a novice prize at Thirsk over 7f last time out, but whether dropping back to today's shorter trip suits is the key question here — the step up to 7f clearly brought improvement, and there may well be more to come from an attractively bred sort.

runners_data.name: Alpe d'Huez
runners_data.note: Archie Watson has a strong record in juvenile sprints and this horse won over 6f on Standard before placing on Soft — goes best up with the pace but the density of prominent types means he may be closer to midfield than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a win last time before confirming debut level with a second at Epsom latest, and acts on the going and has form over the trip — but that Epsom run suggests more is still needed before this one peaks.

runners_data.name: Boleto
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's once-raced winner over 6f Good brings solid juvenile credentials — wants to race prominently off the pace but must contest that position with several equally-qualified rivals, so his final finishing position may not reflect his natural style.|
runners_data.comment: Boleto won a maiden at Pontefract on debut 15 days ago, hitting the line well over today's trip on good ground, and open to further progress for a top yard — though stepping up sharply in grade from a single start leaves plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Celeron
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on M D O'Callaghan's unbeaten 6f Good winner — naturally prominent but the field's composition will likely deny him that ground, making his true chance harder to assess from the map position alone.|
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye winning on debut at the Curragh two weeks ago, hitting the line well over today's trip on good to yielding, and a respected juvenile handler suggests there's more to come — though stepping up to this level from a single start leaves questions unanswered.

runners_data.name: Charted Course
runners_data.note: Fahey stable's runner was second on Soft over 6f in limited experience — unknown style flags limited confidence in what shape suits him best, with jockey James Doyle providing the clearest upgrade angle.|
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on debut at Haydock, runner-up after racing keen on soft, and today's drier conditions look a clear step in the right direction — winless in recent starts but capable of outrunning odds if settling better over this trip.

runners_data.name: Dance A Jig
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett filly has twice finished second at 5f on Good and Soft — a genuine pace-positive type whose redistribution into midfield reflects the field dynamics rather than her own preference, and she may find traffic a problem.|
runners_data.comment: Consecutive runner-up finishes suggest Dance A Jig has plenty of ability yet to convert, and a step up to today's 6f looks a logical move for this useful maiden — though 47 days off and winless in recent starts means there are still questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Dorigo
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 6f Standard runner-up has unknown natural style and has been mapped further back than his instinct might prefer because the hold-up positions need populating — treat his rear position with caution.|
runners_data.comment: Showed plenty of pace on debut when runner-up at Newcastle, but that sole start leaves improvement needed to trouble these at a ranking of 21 of 25, and the step up in grade makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Green Sovereign
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's colt won over 6f Soft before a 5th on Standard — one of the prominent runners best placed to actually secure a forward position given draw and muted redistribution, making him tactically well-situated.|
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by six lengths on good-to-soft at Pontefract last time, hitting the line strongly for a trainer in form, and a top rider retains the mount on a lightly raced type with more improvement to come; the 5th on debut is the only blot, though that now reads like a learning run.

runners_data.name: Ischgl
runners_data.note: Three consistent 6f placings for Ciaran Murphy's horse, all on Good or Soft ground — a genuine traveller with the experience to handle a big field and one of the more reliable prominent-positioned types in this race.|
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when runner-up at Listowel 17 days ago and acts on today's conditions, but winless in its last three starts and, despite useful ability with debut form franked at Group level, looks vulnerable to find a win here.

runners_data.name: King Of Cloughan
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's colt has twice placed on Good at 6-7f — unknown style with light experience, and the 33-day absence alongside an unproven going profile adds modest doubt to his readiness.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, King Of Cloughan does at least arrive on the back of a promising second at Leopardstown over today's trip, beaten only three-quarters of a length, and a top yard keeps the faith from stall 22.

runners_data.name: One Number
runners_data.note: O'Brien's once-raced runner-up over 6f Good carries a strong booking in Dylan Browne McMonagle — races prominently and has the profile to hold that berth given only two prior outings, keeping him straightforward to assess.|
runners_data.comment: Promising on debut, finishing runner-up beaten two lengths at the Curragh over today's trip, and that late-running style suits; yet to win in recent starts and breaking from stall 10 is a neutral factor, though improvement looks possible on good-to-yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Our Boy Bailey
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's runner was second over 8f Good on debut — the step down to 6f is a notable query and while the prominent style is suitable, the trip shortfall makes him one of the more speculative runners in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on debut, rallying to finish a close second at Roscommon, but a drop in trip from that 7f effort looks a concern here, and from draw 21 carrying 128lb, this winless runner ranks 19th on our figures in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Control
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's winner over 5f Handicap (AW) returns after 94 days — the long layoff is the headline concern, and the step to 6f turf from all-weather sprinting makes this a significant test of adaptability.|
runners_data.comment: Opened her account with a head victory in a strong Curragh maiden on debut and should improve again stepping up in trip today — the main concern is a 94-day absence since that encouraging first start.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's colt won over 5f Good on debut with Oisin Murphy — the step to 6f is the key query, but Palmer knows the Ascot juvenile sprint well and the top jockey booking suggests the stable is confident about the distance.|
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by three lengths on debut at Hamilton and shaped like a smart prospect, with today's trip and conditions well within range; the wide draw in this big field is the one unknown.

runners_data.name: Sergei Diaghilev
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's unbeaten 6f Good winner with Ryan Moore aboard — the standout jockey-trainer combination in the race, and the horse's natural prominent style is well-suited to tracking Wild Terrain and producing a decisive move.|
runners_data.comment: Bolted up on debut at the Curragh, hitting the line strongly to win by half a length, and now steps up from that promising maiden success with a top jockey aboard and a yard that has won this race twice since 2019 — very much the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Victory Gold
runners_data.note: Saeed bin Suroor's horse wears headgear and has twice placed on Good over 6f — two placed runs show consistent form but no win yet on turf, and the prominent style at least keeps him in the race without needing the pace to be extreme.|
runners_data.comment: Hood goes on for the first time as Victory Gold lines up winless in recent starts, but there's encouragement from a debut second and the step back to 6f on a sound surface suits; that fourth at Leicester latest, beaten 5½ lengths, leaves improvement needed from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's confirmed front-runner wears a hood and won on Good over 6f before a debut 12th on Soft — clearly best on Good or faster and perfectly placed tactically as the lone pace-setter, though the STYLE_FIT flag signals he is at his best when allowed to bowl along freely rather than when pressured.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in grade last time and beaten well at Epsom, Wild Terrain heads here ranked bottom of the field on our figures and debuts in blinkers — though a recent win and proven stamina over today's trip offer slim crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Controlla
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's runner was second on Good over 6f on debut — unknown style in a small sample with limited market depth, and the 31-day absence alongside a below-par trainer strike rate keeps expectations modest.|
runners_data.comment: Controlla shaped with plenty of promise on debut, going down by only a neck in a Group 3 Fillies' Sprint Stakes at Naas, and acts on good ground over today's trip — yet to score in recent starts but open to improvement and merits respect from stall 15 carrying 123lb.

runners_data.name: Freedom Flame
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' horse won over 6f Good before a 4th on Standard — wears headgear and is a natural pace-positive runner who is displaced into midfield purely by field congestion, not by any lack of early speed in his own right.|
runners_data.comment: Freedom Flame confirmed debut level when winning a maiden by a neck last time but that form needs marked progress to threaten here; first-time hood is the one intriguing angle, though our figures rank this 24th of 25 runners.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's hold-up juvenile placed at 5f Good and 7f Standard — one of only a handful of true hold-up types in the race, needs the pace to be genuinely strong and gaps to open late over a trip that looks on the sharp side.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked 20th of 25 on our figures, Harlequin Sky faces a stiff ask at this level. She was hampered late at Wolverhampton 19 days ago and arguably ran better than the bare result suggests, but looks a long shot here despite proven ability at today's trip.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's once-raced winner on Standard over 6f with P J McDonald — limited form to assess on turf but the trainer is in solid form (T14: 8/64) and a debut win over this trip is a clean foundation.|
runners_data.comment: Debut winner at Kempton over today's trip on AW, scoring with plenty in hand, and the yard excels here — Moonrise looks a smart prospect with obvious claims, though a first run beyond novice company at stall 14 off 123lb will test how far that debut form stretches.

runners_data.name: On The Queue Tee
runners_data.note: J S Moore's hold-up runner has twice placed over 5f Good — the hold-up style is genuine but the step up in grade to Listed level and the trip extension to 6f both require confirmation of ability.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last two starts and ranked 22 of 25 on our figures, On The Queue Tee faces a stiff step up in class from novice company at Bath — effective over the trip on a sound surface, but the form book offers little encouragement against this field.

runners_data.name: Troublesome Guest
runners_data.note: George Margarson's debutant third over 6f Good — unknown style with only one run, an out-of-form trainer (T14: 0/7) and light experience against more seasoned juveniles makes this a significant ask.|
runners_data.comment: Showed promise on debut with a Newmarket third beaten two lengths, and has the right profile at 6f on good — but winless in recent starts and looks up against it stepping into this grade from stall 24.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Terrain is the confirmed pace-setter and will break from the gates to lead on a flat, right-handed track where Good to Firm conditions reward a clean, uncontested gallop. With only one confirmed front-runner, the pace is likely to be honest but not brutal — Wild Terrain can dictate terms without being harried, which historically at Ascot over 6f creates a steady early clip that turns into a genuine test in the final two furlongs. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses capable of travelling prominently or just off the leader, allowing them to respond when the pace lifts from the 2f pole; true hold-up horses will find little cover in a largely inexperienced 2yo field and will be relying on late gaps that may not materialise. The field contains significantly more prominent-running types than can realistically secure their natural position — Sergei Diaghilev, Sale Shark, Green Sovereign and Ischgl are best placed to claim prominent berths from their draws, while Agitator, Alfred Wallace, Alpe d'Huez, Boleto, Celeron, Dance A Jig and Freedom Flame are likely to be shuffled into midfield against their instincts.

watchPoints.text: Sergei Diaghilev (Ryan Moore, A P O'Brien) is unbeaten over 6f Good and likely to be ridden to take a prominent position behind Wild Terrain — the combination of pace, jockey and course form makes him the most dangerous horse in the race if he travels smoothly.|

Wild Terrain's true front-running role is uncontested but the STYLE_FIT flag means any challenger for the early lead — even a reluctant one from the redistributed prominent types — could unsettle his rhythm and collapse Scenario B.|

The sheer volume of redistributed prominent runners (Agitator, Alfred Wallace, Alpe d'Huez, Boleto, Celeron, Dance A Jig, Freedom Flame) creates a highly congested midfield pack — traffic trouble and interference from 2f home is a genuine risk for any horse trapped in the mass.|

Sale Shark steps up from 5f to 6f for the first time; Oisin Murphy's booking and Hugo Palmer's Ascot knowledge are positives, but the unproven stamina at this trip is the single biggest variable in his chance — watch the market for late confidence signals.|

Ruler's Control returns after 94 days and steps from All-Weather to turf — if he moves freely in the market despite the layoff, the yard may have him very fit, but the absence combined with the surface switch makes him the most logistically uncertain runner in the field.|
